description_full: Duni AB (publ) develops, manufactures, and sells concepts and products for the serving, take-away, and packaging of meals in Sweden, Poland, and internationally. Its products include napkins, table coverings, take away boxes and bowls, take away bags and wraps, plates, amuse bouche and cutlery products, and cups and glasses; reusable products; and candles, LED lamps, and lights, dining solutions, tabletop accessories, sealable packaging and hygiene products, and gift bags and wrappings. The company offers its products under the Duni, Duniform, Paper+Design, EFF, Unmo, Rexcell, Decent Packaging, Relevo, Huskee, Poppies, and BioPak brands. The company offers its products to hotels, restaurants, events and catering, café, public, grocery, and retail sectors; and ready-to-eat meals and take-away applications. Duni AB (publ) was founded in 1949 and is headquartered in Malmö, Sweden.

financial_summary: DUNI AB is a small-cap consumer cyclical business with a $423M market cap on $777M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +4% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.

Returns on capital run at 9% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, and 23% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $19M in free cash flow — roughly 2 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.40× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.8× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 7.5×.

Management returns a meaningful 5.6% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 53% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
